predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: 'the districts of Iraq and al-Ahwaz' near Basra, where the revolt began

successors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
successors.text: Basra, al-Ahwaz and the marshlands, retaken when al-Mukhtarah fell in August 883

ledger.x: 869: the Zanj revolt begins near Basra.
869: fighting for Basra and al-Ahwaz opens.
870: the rebels take al-Ubulla, the port by Basra.
876: the rebels take the marshes between Basra and Wasit.
883: al-Mukhtarah falls and the Zanj hold ends.
883: the fighting ends with the fall of al-Mukhtarah.
883: the Zanj state ends; its land returns to the Abbasid caliph.

wars.name: Zanj Rebellion
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory: al-Ubulla 870, Suq al-Ahwaz and Basra 871, the marshes 876, furthest extent 879, government counteroffensive from late 879, al-Mukhtarah besieged February 881 and fallen August 883.

certainty.note: Districts and cities only; no boundary is on the page.
